source_refs.note: Topic 2.9.1, printed pages 40-41: configurations of ions, including the d block rule.

blocks.text: Positive ions form when electrons are removed from atoms. The sodium ion Na+ (proton number 11) has 10 electrons, so its configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p6, the same as neon, the element with 10 electrons in each atom. Negative ions form when atoms gain electrons. The sulfide ion S2- (proton number 16) has 18 electrons and the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, the same as argon.

In general the electrons of the outer subshell are removed when metal atoms form positive ions, but the d block elements behave slightly differently. Reading across the table from potassium to zinc the 4s subshell fills before the 3d subshell, yet when atoms of a d block element lose electrons to form ions the 4s electrons are lost first. A titanium atom is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d2 4s2 and the Ti2+ ion 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d2; a chromium atom is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d5 4s1 and the Cr3+ ion 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d3.
